title: Artifact host policy: tracking server refuses host-addressed artifact URIs (ftp, sftp, hdfs, viewfs, http/https, mlflow-artifacts, r2, b2, abfss) unless they target the server's default artifact root or artifacts destination host, or the scheme is opted in via MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES
answers: Why does creating an experiment with an ftp or hdfs artifact_location now return a 400 on my tracking server?
How do I allow experiments or model versions to store artifacts on a second HDFS or SFTP host that is not the default artifact root?
Where is the check that stops the server from connecting to an arbitrary host named in a stored artifact location?
Why does a model version source on an http or mlflow-artifacts URI get rejected when registering from a client?
body:
Path: Server-side acceptance and fetch of artifact locations: experiment artifact_location, workspace default_artifact_root and trace archival location (via _validate_storage_location_uri), model version source (_create_model_version), and stored run, model version, logged model and trace locations on fetch. The chokepoint for the decision is mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:rejected_host_addressed_scheme.
Rule: A host-addressed URI is accepted only if its targets (scheme family, lowercased hostname, effective port) match the server's own --default-artifact-root or --artifacts-destination (read from the _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_ROOT / _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_DESTINATION env markers), or its scheme is listed in mlflow/environment_variables.py:MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES. Ports are normalized to each scheme's well-known port before comparing; viewfs is grouped with hdfs, https and mlflow-artifacts with http; an authority containing a backslash or whitespace is never trusted. Any new code path that resolves a stored location must go through the same policy rather than a bare get_artifact_repository call.
Symptom: A client could make the tracking server open connections to arbitrary hosts and ports by naming them in an experiment location, model version source, or workspace storage setting (GHSA-mr9f-g8qf-4w4j).
Constraints: Standard deployments whose artifacts live on the server's own storage host see no change. Multi-server setups keep working when the tracking server's default root points at the artifacts server. Non-host schemes (s3, gs, file, local paths) are not affected. Workspace default roots on a different host than the server's are rejected unless the scheme is opted in. Client processes (no server marker) are not checked by the registry; only the server handlers and server-side jobs are.
applies: Tracking server artifact location validation and fetch for host-addressed schemes; not applicable to client-only processes or to cloud-bucket schemes.
says: Creating an experiment pointing to a remote file server fails with a bad request error.
Registering a model version from an external web address is rejected by the server.
Allow saving experiment runs and models to a secondary network storage host.
Workspace storage settings reject custom network storage locations outside the default server host.
Cannot download or view logged run artifacts stored on remote network servers.
search: Tracking server artifact host policy in mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:rejected_host_addressed_scheme and mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_artifact_uri_scheme rejects host-addressed artifact URIs unless they match the server's --default-artifact-root or --artifacts-destination, or the scheme is listed in MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES. It validates experiment artifact_location, workspace default_artifact_root, trace archival location, model version source, and stored locations on fetch by comparing normalized scheme families, lowercased hostnames, and effective ports. Non-host schemes like s3, gs, and local file paths are unaffected, and client-only processes without server markers are not checked by the registry.
